subject: short-tailed shrew
title: A Venomous Shrew Paralyzes Its Prey and Keeps It Alive for 15 Days

scenes.text: This mouse-sized mammal is venomous. And it keeps a living pantry.
The northern short-tailed shrew has no fangs. Its lower front teeth are grooved, and venom runs down the groove with every bite.
Within minutes the bitten snail, beetle or mouse stops moving. Not dead. Paralyzed.
The shrew drags it underground and stacks it in a larder. In one study it hoarded about 87 percent of everything it caught.
A paralyzed mealworm stayed alive and fresh in a shrew's cache for up to fifteen days.
One shrew carries enough venom to take down around 200 mice. A four-inch animal, with a fridge that breathes.

description:
The northern short-tailed shrew is one of the few venomous mammals. Its saliva carries a neurotoxin that flows down grooves in its lower incisors and paralyzes prey within minutes.
Instead of eating everything at once, the shrew stores the paralyzed animals underground: one study found it cached about 87 percent of its catch, and a paralyzed mealworm can stay alive for up to 15 days. The US National Park Service notes one shrew may carry enough venom to kill around 200 mice.
Would you rather be eaten fast or kept in the pantry? Comment below.
first_comment: Its eyes are the size of poppy seeds and barely work, so it finds prey partly by echolocation, like a very bad bat. Which venomous animal should we cover next?
